103: ## 3. Power Supply
104: 
105: In Phase 0/1 the logger is powered **from USB-C only** (§5.3). The buck
106: converter described here is first used on the passive tap board (PR-04a) and
107: then on the intercept board.
108: 
109: ### 3.1 Source
110: 
111: The bike's 9V DC power supply (YINGJIAO YS25-0903000, 9V/3A) enters the
112: frame and travels up to the console via the 9-pin loom (White = +9V,
113: Brown = GND). The passive tap and intercept boards tap this 9V rail.
114: 
115: ### 3.2 Regulation
116: 
117: A GTIWUNG MP1584EN adjustable buck converter steps 9V down to 3.3V.
118: Whether the Waveshare board's VIN pin can take 9V directly (removing the
119: external buck for the SoC) is Phase 0 register row 11, decided at DR-1.
120: 
121: ```
122: J1 Pin 8 (White, +9V) ───────────────────────────┐
123:                                                    │
124: J1 Pin 9 (Brown, GND) ────────────────────────┐   │
125:                                                │   │
126:                                     ┌──────────┤───┤──────────────┐
127:                                     │  U3      │   │              │
128:                                     │  MP1584EN GND  VIN          │
129:                                     │          │                  │
130:                                     │          │   VOUT ──────────┼──► 3.3V RAIL
131:                                     │          │   (set via       │
132:                                     │          │    trimpot)      │
133:                                     └──────────┤──────────────────┘
134:                                                │
135:                                                ▼
136:                                            COMMON GND
137: ```
138: 
139: > [!IMPORTANT]
140: > **Before connecting any load**, power the MP1584EN from 9V with the output
141: > disconnected. Measure the output with a multimeter and adjust the blue
142: > trimpot until it reads **3.3V ± 0.05V**. Then connect loads. The ESP32-S3
143: > absolute maximum is 3.6V; on a vibrating bike, fix the trimpot (glue) or
144: > replace it with fixed resistors `[DR-1]` (audit H-03).
145: 
146: ### 3.3 Rail Distribution
147: 
148: On the passive tap board, the 3.3V rail powers only U1. On the intercept
149: board it is distributed as follows (**PROVISIONAL `[DR-1]`**):
150:

152: 3.3V RAIL ──┬──► U1 ESP32-S3-Nano pin 2 (3V3) — direct to SoC
153:             │
154:             ├──► SW1 ─► R3 (10kΩ) ──► Cadence pull-up (standalone only)
155:             │
156:             ├──► SW2 ─► R4 (100Ω) ──► Pot reference (standalone only)
157:             │
158:             └──► SW4 ─► R5 (10Ω) ──► Encoder power (standalone only)

160: MOTOR RAIL [DR-1: D3] ──► U2 motor driver supply (separate from the SoC rail)

166: |---|---|---|---|---|
167: | ESP32-S3 (WiFi + BLE active) | 200 mA | 500 mA | Continuous | All |

176: driver** (current limit and fault output, e.g. DRV8833 or TB6612) rather than

180: ### 3.5 USB-C Power and Programming
181: 
182: - **Phase 0/1 (breadboard observer) and Phase 2 (HR-only):** USB-C is the
183:   only power source. There is no buck converter to disconnect, and the
184:   logger can be flashed at any time without rewiring.
185: - **Buck-powered boards (passive tap and intercept):** the USB port feeds
186:   the ESP32's VBUS, and the onboard LDO produces a second 3.3V source on the

190: > On a buck-powered board, **disconnect the buck converter's output** (or
191: > its 9V input) before plugging in USB-C. Two regulators on one 3.3V rail can
192: > cause droop or overshoot. Routine updates on installed boards use **manual
193: > OTA** (enabled and tested in PR-04a), so USB is a recovery path only.

287: ### 5.2 Motor-Drive Characterisation Gate
288: 
289: > [!CAUTION]
290: > **Complete this before connecting the motor-sense taps (GPIO 6/7).** The
291: > other taps may be connected immediately. This gate **characterises** the
292: > drive; it does not expect a particular answer.
293: 
294: A DMM measured **3.3V** on the motor wires, but a DMM shows the *average*
295: voltage — it cannot distinguish 3.3V DC from 9V PWM at ~37% duty cycle.
296: The ÷4 divider (§5.4) keeps the ESP32 pin below 3.3V for any drive up to
297: about 13V, so **either result lets logging proceed**. The captures are
298: evidence for Phase 0 register row 1 and feed DR-1 (sense network, relay
299: logic, motor rail).
300: 
301: **Setup:** DC coupling, 5V/div. Scope ground to Brown (via the harness).
302: CH1 on Red (motor +), CH2 on Black (motor −). If the scope has math, also
303: display CH1 − CH2.
304: 
305: **Captures (save each as an evidence file, §5.2.2):**
306: 
307: | # | Condition | Timebase | What to record |
308: |---|---|---|---|
309: | 1 | At rest (no knob movement, bike powered) | 10 ms/div | Both wires: driven low (brake), floating (coast), or other |
310: | 2 | Knob one click **up** | 10 ms/div | Drive duration, which wire is high, levels |
311: | 3 | Knob one click **down** | 10 ms/div | As #2, opposite direction |
312: | 4 | Knob up, during drive | µs/div (e.g. 10 µs/div) | Flat DC, or PWM (frequency, duty, peak) |
313: | 5 | Knob down, during drive | µs/div | As #4 |
314: | 6 | Drive end (either direction) | 10 ms/div, then µs/div | Braking, coasting, back-EMF excursions below GND |
315: 
316: ```
317: Flat DC drive:                      PWM drive:
318:     ┌────┐                              ┌┐ ┌┐ ┌┐ ┌┐
319:  V  │    │                           V  ││ ││ ││ ││
320:     │    │                              ││ ││ ││ ││
321: ────┘    └──────────── 0V          ─────┘└─┘└─┘└─┘└──── 0V
322: ```
323: 
324: **Outcomes:**
325: 
326: - **Flat DC (≈3.3V):** the divider output is ≈0.825V, at the ESP32-S3's
327:   V_IL maximum — not a valid logic HIGH. Motor sense is sampled as analog on
328:   ADC1.
329: - **PWM (any amplitude up to ~13V):** the divider still protects the pin
330:   (9V ÷ 4 = 2.25V). Record frequency, duty and peak; burst capture
331:   (1–5 kHz) and threshold-based drive detection handle it in firmware.
332: - **Peak above ~12V (not expected):** stop, and resize the divider before
333:   connecting GPIO 6/7.

422: ### 5.4 Motor Sense Voltage Dividers (R1a/R1b, R2a/R2b)
423: 
424: The motor is driven bidirectionally by the console's H-bridge — Red goes HIGH
425: while Black goes LOW (forward), then the reverse for backward. Back-EMF when
426: the motor stops can also push wires below ground.
427: 
428: The 30kΩ + 10kΩ divider is **protection and scaling only**, not a
429: logic-level interface:

431: ```

433:                                 │
434:                             R1b/R2b (10kΩ)
435:                                 │
436:                                GND

438: Division ratio: 10k / (30k + 10k) = 1/4   → pin stays ≤ 3.3V up to ~13V drive

459: ### 5.5 Direct-Tap Series Resistors (RS1–RS8) and the No-Pulls Rule
460: 
461: The eight direct taps (every tap except GPIO 6/7) each have a **4.7 kΩ series
462: resistor**, placed at the harness end of the tail.
463: 
464: > [!IMPORTANT]
465: > **Bench-tested 2026-10-03:** The original 22 kΩ value exceeded the ESP32-S3
466: > ADC continuous-mode source-impedance limit (Espressif recommends < 10 kΩ).
467: > At 83 kHz aggregate sample rate the S/H capacitor could not settle through
468: > 22 kΩ during brief reed-switch closures (~50 ms). Replaced with 4.7 kΩ +
469: > 100 nF ceramic cap on the ESP32 side. Cadence detection confirmed at
470: > 74–120 RPM.
471: 
472: **Why — back-powering.** Each ESP32 pad has ESD clamp diodes to its 3.3V
473: supply. If the ESP32 is unpowered (USB unplugged, or during boot/brown-out)
474: while the console is on, the console's 3.3V lines — pot reference (Yellow),
475: wiper (Blue), encoder VCC and channels, cadence — would drive current
476: through those diodes into the ESP32's rail and try to power it. That loads
477: the pot reference and the encoder supply, which are exactly what register
478: rows 4, 6, 8 and 10 measure, and can disturb the console. 4.7 kΩ limits any
479: such current to about 0.7 mA, which is still low enough to avoid measurably
480: loading the console's lines.
481: 
482: **No pulls.** Every tap pin is configured with **no internal pull-up or
483: pull-down**. An internal pull (~45 kΩ) on a cadence or encoder pin would bias
484: the console's own line and change what is being measured.
485: 
486: **Decoupling capacitor (C1).** A 100 nF ceramic capacitor is placed between
487: each ADC signal pin and GND on the ESP32 side of the series resistor. This
488: provides a low-impedance charge reservoir for the ADC's sample-and-hold
489: capacitor, ensuring accurate readings even with the 4.7 kΩ source impedance.

706: #### 7.3.2 Why the Motor Wires Are Split
707: 
708: In the stock bike, the console drives the motor directly via pins 1–2
709: of the 9-pin loom. The intercept board breaks this connection:
710: 
711: - **Bike side** (J1 pins 1–2): Motor wires connect to **L9110S outputs**
712:   (A-OA, A-OB), not to J2.
713: - **Console side** (J2 pins 1–2): Console's motor drive signals connect to
714:   **ESP32 ADC1 inputs** (GPIO 6/7) via **voltage dividers** (R1a/R1b,
715:   R2a/R2b).
716: 
717: The console *thinks* it's driving the motor. Actually, its motor signals are
718: read by the ESP32, which decides whether to relay them (Intercept Mode) or
719: ignore them (Override Mode).
720: 
721: #### 7.3.3 Console Motor Sense — Voltage Dividers (R1a/R1b, R2a/R2b)
722: 
723: The same 30kΩ/10kΩ ÷4 divider as Phase 0 (§5.4) scales the console's motor
724: drive for GPIO 6/7. It is not a pull-down and not a logic-level interface;
725: the sensed voltage is read as analog on ADC1.
726: 
727: Two additional benefits on the intercept board:
728: 
729: 1. **Defined idle state**: the divider's R1b/R2b (10kΩ to GND) hold GPIO 6/7
730:    at 0V when the console is not driving.
731: 
732: 2. **Clean disconnect**: In standalone Override (UC6), the console JST is
733:    unplugged and R1b/R2b hold GPIO 6/7 at GND — no floating inputs.
734: 
735: > [!WARNING]
736: > **Fail-safe requirement:** In Intercept Mode, if the ESP32 crashes, the motor is orphaned. A fail-safe mechanism (e.g. NC relay or analog switch bypass) is recommended. Strategy deferred to `[DR-1: decision H-05]`.
